newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen consolidating at around 123.00.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen consolidating at around 123.00.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is likely to consolidate at around 123.00 on Monday.

Some traders said the key U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yield's fall to a three-month low of 6.78 percent on Friday may encourage buying of JGBs. But others said the September's topside is seen capped at last week's high of 123.06 because sharp rises on Wall Street on Friday are expected to boost Tokyo stocks on Monday.
"A focus will be on whether the September rises above 123.06 or not," said a dealer at a "Big Four" brokerage house.
"If it fails to rise above that, it may reverse direction after Friday's gains (in Tokyo and London)," he said.
Traders said the September is likely to move between 122.70 and 123.20 on Monday after finishing at 122.84 on Friday in Tokyo. Later on Friday, it advanced to end at 122.91 on LIFFE.
"Once the contract decides to stay above or below 123.00, I don't see any big factor to make it fluctuate more than 0.30 today," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd is to announce its prime lending rate for June during the day. It is widely expected to be set at 3.1 percent, unchanged from May, traders said.
